Composite 10 components · 3 sections
Complex parts composed from Basic components
Basic, Composite, and which to make
  • Basic components stand alone. A Basic contains no other component: its markup uses only its own classes plus foundation classes such as ds-icon, ds-text-* and the layout classes. Buttons, fields, pills, cards, rows, avatars, code blocks and tables are Basic.
  • Composite components are complex parts composed from Basic components and foundations. A Composite declares every component it uses in uses:, uses each through its declared variants, and adds new markup only for its own __parts where no Basic covers the need. Its CSS lays children out (display, gap, grid, order, alignment, size) and styles only its own parts; it never restyles a component it uses. A Composite may use another Composite only when that one is built solely from Basic components: one level deep, with no cycles.
  • Make the smallest change, in this order: use a declared variant; add a variant to an existing Basic; compose Basic components (inside a screen when the arrangement is one-off, as a Composite when it repeats or is a recognisable pattern); and only when no Basic covers the primitive, add a new Basic. Variant before component; composition before a new Basic.
  • When a Composite needs a look a Basic does not have, the look is added to that Basic as a declared variant first. The Composite never styles around it.
